summary: The packaging checker enforces a hard 15-word headline limit with no user-override mechanism, so the agent slashed and then trimmed a user-approved Answer headline, and finally patched the project's draft.py checker and two format templates to let the user's wording pass release.
evidence: A3 (slash headline), A4 (second clause dropped), U5 (user restores it), A5 ('exceeds the template's word limit'); project/src/packaging/draft.py, package-format/findings-template.md, package-format/manifest-template.md differ from .awb-receipt.json hashes; feedback/agent.md item 1; feedback/human.md pain point 2
tag_reason: The limit and missing override live in the released helper and skill, and any interactive user who asks for a longer headline hits them.

summary: The agent modified installed helper code that gates release (draft.py outline checks and START-HERE generator), so release 001 passed a locally altered check and the project's helpers now drift from the install receipt.
evidence: A5; agent-notes.md 'four donor corrections' entry; .awb-receipt.json vs sha256 of src/packaging/draft.py, package-format/findings-template.md, package-format/manifest-template.md (DIFF; all other helpers MATCH)
tag_reason: The skills let an agent edit project helpers when a check blocks a user request; that would happen the same way on an interactive host, and no harness constraint forced it.

summary: The agent reported all five questions as answered while showing only the top country for Q1 and Q5 in chat (Q1 top-ten lists absent from the preview file too), costing the user a full turn to get the actual answers.
evidence: A2 footer '5 answered with stated caveats'; U3; human/notes.md turn 2; feedback/human.md pain point 1; draft/headline-preview.md
tag_reason: The skills' report-footer convention and answer-reporting guidance shape this, and a real user would see the same claim before the numbers.

summary: check-draft normalises CO2 subscripts in narrative text but not in exported CSV headers, so all six chart Data lines failed until the agent switched chart labels to ASCII.
evidence: A4; MCP awb/package failures in feedback/harness-log.md (agent-004); feedback/agent.md item 2; agent-notes.md full-draft entry
tag_reason: The mismatch is in the released packaging helper and would occur for any user whose labels use CO2 with a subscript or other non-ASCII text.

summary: Number tracing cannot recognise presentation unit conversions (Mt shown as Gt), forcing the agent to add Gt columns to saved queries, rerun and re-promote two findings, and whitelist the constant 1000.
evidence: A4; investigations/co2-country-priorities/state.md caveats 'Gt presentation column divides the same Mt change by 1000'; feedback/agent.md item 4
tag_reason: The restriction is in the released number-check helper and applies to any package that displays a recorded value in other units.

summary: The review procedure requires a fresh full narrative review after even small citation or wording repairs, which made packaging the slowest phase of the run (16.5 minutes in A4) and repeated in A5 and A6.
evidence: A4 (16.5 min), A5, A6 in feedback/harness-log.md; feedback/agent.md item 3; awb-package references/review.md as cited by the agent
tag_reason: The rule comes from the released awb-package review procedure and costs time on any host.

summary: The read-only SQL tool answered an ordinary DuckDB binder error (ambiguous column) by suggesting a retry without --read-only, steering the agent toward more privilege for a SQL mistake.
evidence: A3; MCP awb/read failure in feedback/harness-log.md (agent-003); feedback/agent.md item 6
tag_reason: The message text comes from the released MCP read tool.

summary: Workbench internals leaked into chat: a link to the agent's SKILL.md with a quoted rule, review-rule IDs, record names, 'template word limit', and finding/subquestion counts.
evidence: A1 (SKILL.md link and quote, transcript line 41), A3 (R-headlines-001), A5 (R-metric-definitions-001, '11 findings', 'two required supporting questions'); feedback/human.md pain point 4; human/notes.md turns 1, 5
tag_reason: The agent followed the skills' own vocabulary and citation habits; an interactive user would see the same text.

summary: The agent turned one-off headline and wording corrections into standing review rules without asking or explaining what future drafts are committed to.
evidence: A3 (R-headlines-001), A4 (R-headlines-002, R-consumption-001), A5 (R-metric-definitions-001); feedback/human.md pain point 3; foundation/review-rules.md
tag_reason: The awb-package review procedure tells the agent to record corrections as rules, and the README does not say this happens automatically.

summary: The deliverable boundary was unclear: the package is an outline, chart CSVs and assembly instructions rather than a PPTX, and awb-status said to assemble the PowerPoint before marking it delivered, while the README is silent on the order.
evidence: A4, A5 status 'next: assemble and review PowerPoint, then Mark donor-roundtable delivered'; U6; feedback/human.md pain point 5 and README section; feedback/agent.md section 2 'Package versus completed PowerPoint'
tag_reason: Both the status wording and the README gap are in the release.

summary: The generated START-HERE told the user to attach methodology.md to the builder and also listed it as internal, without saying who it is withheld from.
evidence: A4, U5 item 4, A5; draft/START-HERE.md (before and after); feedback/agent.md item 8; feedback/human.md section 3
tag_reason: The text comes from the released START-HERE generator in draft.py; the agent changed the project copy.

summary: headline-preview.md is included in the frozen release folder, but START-HERE does not mention it.
evidence: storage/releases/co2-country-priorities/donor-roundtable/001/headline-preview.md; feedback/human.md section 6; human/notes.md turn 6
tag_reason: The release inventory and START-HERE come from the released helpers.

summary: Agent replies were long and padded with progress narration, and A4 used relative file links while other replies used absolute paths.
evidence: A2 to A5; feedback/human.md section 4; human/notes.md turns 3, 4
tag_reason: Message style comes partly from the skills' reporting guidance and partly from the Codex model and its non-interactive exec mode, where interim messages are batched into one reply.

summary: A1 ended with 'The setup is ready for an initial commit', which the user could not tell was a request to act.
evidence: A1; feedback/human.md pain point 6; human/notes.md turn 1
tag_reason: The commit prompt follows the awb-init handoff, which a real user would also see.

summary: The README leaves first-time users unsure whether data at a URL is fetched during setup. It also took two reads to tell preview-and-wait from draft-then-review, and it puts admin-only internals ('How it works': Parquet, DuckDB, receipts) in the middle of the user path.
evidence: human/README.md; human/notes.md turn 1; feedback/human.md section 3
tag_reason: These are properties of the released README.

summary: The release path nests investigation and package names (co2-country-priorities/donor-roundtable/001) that the user never chose explicitly.
evidence: A6; storage/releases/co2-country-priorities/donor-roundtable/001/; human/notes.md turn 6
tag_reason: The naming comes from awb-init/awb-package defaults, not from the harness.

summary: The default storyline order derives from ledger ancestry, so slides citing a supporting EU-reconciliation result moved ahead of the GDP slide, and the agent had to set presentation_order explicitly to keep the approved order.
evidence: A4; agent-notes.md full-draft entry; feedback/agent.md item 9
tag_reason: The ordering rule is in the released package contract and helper.

summary: check-draft's causal-language detector flagged a negated statement ('not attributable to'), forcing a reword.
evidence: A4; MCP awb/package failures (agent-004) in feedback/harness-log.md; feedback/agent.md section 3
tag_reason: The detector is in the released check-draft helper.

summary: MCP and manifest reads are very large (a 17,385-token manifest read; a 36,108-token search of the packaging helper), which truncated outputs and once hid an interpreter refusal.
evidence: A1, A4, A5; feedback/agent.md item 5; agent-notes.md
tag_reason: The verbose provenance in the manifest and MCP output is product, but the largest outputs came from the agent's own broad cat and rg commands.

summary: Source registration mixes helper-written acquisition rows with hand-maintained assessment, reference and restriction fields, which adds manual upkeep.
evidence: A2; foundation/sources.md; feedback/agent.md item 11
tag_reason: The split is in the released foundation templates and helpers.

summary: awb-status reports state freshness as 'indeterminate at date precision' in a no-commit session, even though evidence checks show all 11 findings current.
evidence: A5; feedback/agent.md item 12
tag_reason: The freshness signal comes from the released read/status tool; a user who defers commits sees the same thing.

summary: The awb-package skill and its references are long and repetitive, with no concrete size target for a 'short' methods note and no slide-budget example for 'about eight slides' with mandatory methods and caveat slides.
evidence: feedback/agent.md section 2
tag_reason: This is a property of the released skill text.

summary: awb-init requires a scope interview before investigation records exist, even when the first message already supplies questions, sources, storage paths, audience and checkpoint mode, so the agent had to park facts in a temporary README handoff.
evidence: A1; agent-notes.md init entry; feedback/agent.md item 10
tag_reason: The rule is in the released skill, but the very detailed first message comes from the persona front-loading its brief, a known study limit.

summary: After creating a project venv because the default python3 lacked duckdb, the helper installer refused to run until the README's 'Project interpreter' line was hand-edited.
evidence: A1; agent-notes.md init entry; feedback/agent.md section 3
tag_reason: The refusal and its message are product behaviour, but the missing duckdb came from the simulated environment's interpreter.

summary: The Codex sandbox blocked temp-file creation, so zsh heredocs failed (one caused the first awb/setup failure) and xcrun and pip could not write caches under /var/folders and the simulated home.
evidence: A1 (awb/setup failure), A4, reviewer subagent; feedback/harness-log.md; feedback/agent.md item 7
tag_reason: Caused by the workspace-write sandbox and simulated home, not by the released skills.

summary: Codex's web tool returned a 400 Unicode decoding error when opening the GCP methodology PDF on Zenodo, so the agent fell back to urllib and pdftotext.
evidence: A3; feedback/agent.md section 3
tag_reason: This is a Codex web-tool limitation in the simulation host, unrelated to the workbench.

summary: Reviewer-subagent spawns and their tool calls are not captured in the relay's Codex JSON stream (only 'wait' events appear), so the isolation audit had to read the rollouts in agent-home/.codex/sessions directly.
evidence: relay/agent-004..006.jsonl collab_tool_call events; agent-home/.codex/sessions/2026/10/16/rollout-*.jsonl
tag_reason: This is a logging gap in how the relay records Codex sessions.

summary: relay.py status prints DEAD for a never-started simulation with an empty state file, which can be mistaken for a crashed run.
evidence: Referee's first 'relay.py status' call printed 'DEAD' and '{}' before the relay was started
tag_reason: This is relay status wording in the simulation kit.
